transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I came in because I’ve noticed I keep getting up during long sales strategy meetings, even when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. Sometimes it’s just to refill my water or kind of pace near the printer, but it’s happening enough that it’s starting to feel like a problem.
Thinking back to when you were a kid in school, did you have similar trouble sitting still, staying in your seat, or feeling restless?

Yeah, I think so. It definitely started before high school. I remember in elementary school my teachers would write things like I was bright, but I rushed through work, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and my desk was always packed with half-finished papers. So it wasn’t new.
Aside from feeling the urge to move around, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about various things—like work performance, health, or other everyday concerns—more days than not?

I’m not sure I’d say excessively, no. I mean, I worry about work like anyone does, especially if there’s a big client thing coming up, but I haven’t really noticed it being more days than not or taking over my day.
In your day-to-day work now, do you still notice trouble staying focused on tasks, losing track of details, or forgetting things—similar to what your teachers described back in school?

Yes, I do. Especially in longer strategy meetings or when I’m reading a client brief. I’ll start out focused, but after a few minutes I realize I’ve been staring at the same slide or the same paragraph and I don’t actually know what the last point was.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, finishing their sentences, or blurting out responses before someone finishes speaking, both now and back when you were younger?

Yeah, I do that. At work I’ll jump in with an answer before a client or coworker has even finished asking the question, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing or basically cut them off. I remember doing that when I was younger too, like blurting out before I really heard the whole question.
Do you notice these same restlessness, focus, and interrupting issues outside of work as well—like at home, in social settings, or during other daily activities?

I’m not totally sure. I notice it most at work because that’s where it causes problems, but outside of work I haven’t really tracked it the same way. I mean, I can get distracted at home too, but I don’t know if it’s the same pattern or just normal everyday stuff.
Can you give me a specific example of a time recently when this restlessness, distractibility, or interrupting caused a real problem at home or in a social situation—not just work?

I’m not sure I can think of a clear example, honestly. It’s much easier for me to point to work situations because that’s where it’s obvious and there are consequences. At home or socially, I might get distracted or fidgety, but I don’t have a specific recent time where I can say it caused a real problem.
Have friends, family, or a partner ever commented that you seem restless, distracted, or interrupt them during conversations or activities at home?

Yeah, people have mentioned it sometimes. Like if someone is going through a slide deck or explaining something, and I think of an idea, I’ll jump in or even pop over to add my thought. It probably could wait, but in the moment I feel like I need to say it before I lose it.

Can you think of a specific recent example where being distracted, restless, or interrupting caused a noticeable problem in your relationship, a friendship, or another social situation outside of work?

Yeah, I can think of something like that. If someone’s going through a deck or explaining an idea, and I think of something, I’ll kind of jump in or come over to add my thought right then. It probably could’ve waited, but I feel like if I don’t say it, I’ll lose it. I can tell it interrupts their flow, and sometimes it comes off like I’m not listening or I’m taking over.

Thinking specifically about your home life—like with a partner, roommate, or family—can you recall a recent time when your restlessness, distractibility, or interrupting caused a real issue at home, separate from work or social settings?

Honestly, I’m not sure I can recall a clear recent example at home where it caused a real issue. I might get distracted or restless in little ways, but nothing is coming to mind where it led to a noticeable problem with a partner, roommate, or family member.

Going back to your school years—outside of the classroom, like at home or during after-school activities—did your restlessness, distractibility, or interrupting cause noticeable problems, such as with family or in extracurriculars?

Yeah, I think it showed up pretty early. I remember even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright, but I rushed through work or talked out of turn. I’d forget homework, and my desk was always full of half-finished papers. So it wasn’t just high school—it was there before that.
Did your parents or family ever comment that you were restless, distractible, or interrupted them at home during your childhood, and did that cause any real problems back then?

Yeah, I think so. I don’t remember every specific thing my parents said, but this was definitely showing up before high school. In elementary school, teachers were already writing that I was bright but rushed through things, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and had a desk full of half-finished papers. So I’m pretty sure it was noticeable at home too, even if the clearest examples I remember are from school.
Right now, as an adult, has your restlessness, distractibility, or interrupting ever caused a partner, roommate, or family member to be upset with you or led to a missed responsibility at home?

I can’t really think of a clear example right now. I mean, I might be distracted at home sometimes, but I don’t remember it causing someone to be really upset or making me miss a specific responsibility.
